description: Defines the structural model of causation, emergence, and abstraction consistency. In the AI Edition, causation is not a primitive — it is a structural relation subject to the same invariant constraints as all other relations. Emergence is the appearance of invariants in a structure S that are absent from its proper sub-structures. Abstraction consistency (INV-NOS-004) governs the downward and upward propagation of invariants between abstract and concrete structural levels.

structural_causation_model.title: Causation as Structural Relation
structural_causation_model.nos_thesis: Causation, under the AI Edition's structural realist commitment, is not a primitive metaphysical force — it is a directed structural relation in the dependency graph of structures. What makes a relation causal, rather than merely associative, is the structural asymmetry and invariant-preservation conditions it satisfies.
structural_causation_model.formal: cause(S_a, S_b) ⟺ (S_a → S_b) ∈ R_world ∧ ¬(S_b → S_a) ∈ R_world ∧ invariant_set(S_b) is partially determined by invariant_set(S_a)

components.directed_asymmetry: Causal relations are asymmetric structural dependencies: S_a → S_b means S_a is in the dependency position, S_b in the dependent position. Structural causation does not admit symmetric cause-effect pairs.
components.invariant_determination: S_a causally contributes to S_b if some invariants of S_b are not satisfiable without S_a's contribution to the relational configuration. This is a structural — not counterfactual — criterion.

causation_types.label: Constitutive Causation
causation_types.description: S_a causally constitutes S_b: S_b's relational configuration includes S_a as a structural component. The causal relation is one of structural participation — S_a is part of what S_b is.
causation_types.formal: constitutive_cause(S_a, S_b) ⟺ S_a ∈ sub(S_b) ∧ remove(S_b, S_a) violates invariant_set(S_b)
causation_types.cross_book: SARG: Evidence nodes constitutively cause the support relation they ground (INV-SARG-002). Remove the Evidence node and the warrant relation loses its grounding — the argument's invariant set is violated.

causation_types.label: Enabling Causation
causation_types.description: S_a enables S_b without being a component of S_b. S_a's existence or state is a precondition for S_b's invariant set to be satisfiable, but S_a is not inside S_b.
causation_types.formal: enabling_cause(S_a, S_b) ⟺ S_a ∉ sub(S_b) ∧ ¬satisfiable(invariant_set(S_b)) without S_a in the structural context
causation_types.cross_book: GRL: Book 1 FFT kernel is an enabling cause of GRL regimes. The regime's invariants are not satisfiable without the FFT primitive definitions — yet FFT is not part of the regime tuple R = ⟨N_R, E_R, C_R, S_R, α_R, λ_R⟩.

causation_types.label: Transformative Causation
causation_types.description: S_a causes a transformation T that produces S_b from an earlier structure S_0. The causal relation is mediated by the transformation event. S_a is the transformation trigger.
causation_types.formal: transformative_cause(S_a, S_0, S_b) ⟺ S_a triggers T ∧ transform(S_0, T) = S_b ∧ ¬(T triggered without S_a)
causation_types.cross_book: OR: An observer's increase in δ (detection capacity) is a transformative cause of the revelation state change in OR-Ρ. The transformation from opaque to revealed is triggered by the observer's capacity change, not by any change in the structure S itself (INV-OR-003 preserved).

emergence_model.title: Structural Emergence
emergence_model.nos_definition: Emergence occurs when a structure S has invariants in its invariant_set(S) that are not present in the invariant sets of any of its proper sub-structures. Emergent invariants are not hidden in the parts — they arise from the relational configuration that assembles the parts into S.
emergence_model.formal: emergent(inv, S) ⟺ inv ∈ invariant_set(S) ∧ ∀s_i ∈ proper_sub(S): inv ∉ invariant_set(s_i)

emergence_levels.label: Weak Emergence
emergence_levels.description: Emergent invariants of S are in principle derivable from the invariant sets of S's sub-structures and the relational configuration that joins them — but the derivation requires complete knowledge of the full configuration. They are not practically predictable from sub-structure analysis alone.
emergence_levels.nos_status: Compatible with structural realism. Weak emergence is a function of relational complexity, not of any ontological novelty.
emergence_levels.example: The regime validity invariant (INV-GRL-001) is weakly emergent from the enforcement relations E_R connecting regime nodes to governed structures. No individual node in N_R satisfies INV-GRL-001 alone — it requires the full configuration.

emergence_levels.label: Strong Emergence
emergence_levels.description: Emergent invariants of S are not derivable from the invariant sets of S's sub-structures and their relational configuration, even in principle. Strong emergence implies genuine ontological novelty at the level of S.
emergence_levels.nos_status: Formally compatible with INV-NOS-004 but constitutes the 'genuine novelty' case: the emergent invariant of S is not present in the abstract structure that S instantiates, triggering the upward revision requirement of INV-NOS-004.
emergence_levels.example: If a governance regime produces a stable legitimacy condition (INV-GRL-004) that cannot be derived from the authority decay model (INV-GRL-002) and constraint enforcement model (INV-GRL-003) — this would be strong emergence requiring GRL abstract revision.

emergence_levels.label: Phantom Emergence
emergence_levels.description: Apparent emergence arising from incomplete invariant specification of sub-structures. The invariant appears emergent because sub-structure invariant sets were not fully declared — not because the invariant is genuinely novel.
emergence_levels.nos_status: Not genuine emergence. Phantom emergence is a modeling error. NoS-Κ (CausationAudit) is responsible for detecting phantom emergence by auditing sub-structure invariant completeness.
emergence_levels.detection: If adding a sub-structure invariant that was previously undeclared dissolves the apparent emergent property, it was phantom emergence. If the property persists even with complete sub-structure invariant declarations, it is genuine (weak or strong) emergence.

abstraction_consistency_mechanics.title: INV-NOS-004 Mechanics — Abstract to Instance
evaluation_procedure: Step 1: Declare S_abstract with its complete invariant_set(S_abstract)
Step 2: Declare S_instance as a claimed instance of S_abstract
Step 5: If ⊆ holds AND invariant_set(S_instance) = invariant_set(S_abstract): valid instance, no novelty
Step 6: If ⊆ holds AND invariant_set(S_instance) ⊃ invariant_set(S_abstract): valid instance with genuine novelty — flag for S_abstract upward revision
Step 7: If ⊆ fails: S_instance is not a valid instance — classify as modeling error or distinct structure

outcome_types.label: Consistent Instance
outcome_types.description: S_instance is a valid instantiation. All abstract invariants hold in the instance. If S_instance has additional invariants, they are genuine novelty and should be examined for upward propagation.
outcome_types.action: Accept instance. If novel invariants present, initiate NoS-Σ upward revision protocol.

outcome_types.label: Modeling Error
outcome_types.condition: ∃inv ∈ invariant_set(S_abstract): inv ∉ invariant_set(S_instance) AND S_instance was intended to instantiate S_abstract
outcome_types.description: The claimed instance violates at least one abstract invariant. This is a modeling error: either S_abstract was misapplied or S_instance was incorrectly formulated.
outcome_types.action: Do not accept instance. Return to SARG (Book 7) for argument reconstruction or to TEL (Book 5) for re-encoding. Identify the violated invariant and trace the modeling error.

outcome_types.label: Genuine Novelty
outcome_types.description: S_instance carries invariants absent from S_abstract. This is not a violation — it is the discovery of structural properties not anticipated by the abstract form. Upward revision of S_abstract is warranted.
outcome_types.action: Accept instance. Flag novel invariants. Initiate upward revision: propose addition of novel invariants to S_abstract, subject to coherence checking against all other declared instances of S_abstract.

upward_revision_protocol.title: Upward Revision under Genuine Novelty
upward_revision_protocol.description: When an instance S_instance exhibits genuine novelty (AC-OUT-003), the novel invariants must be evaluated for inclusion in S_abstract. This is not automatic — novel invariants must be coherent with all existing instances.
steps: Step 1: Identify the set of novel invariants: novel_invs = invariant_set(S_instance) \ invariant_set(S_abstract)
Step 2: Retrieve all declared instances of S_abstract: {S_i : instance(S_i, S_abstract)}
Step 3: For each inv ∈ novel_invs: check that ∀S_i: inv ∈ invariant_set(S_i). If any S_i fails: the novel invariant is instance-specific, not abstract-level.
Step 4: For each universally satisfied novel_inv: propose addition to invariant_set(S_abstract)

Step 5: Apply INV-NOS-003 check: does adding novel_inv to S_abstract change the identity of S_abstract? If invariant_set changes but no prior instance is invalidated: abstract identity is preserved (the abstract structure gained a property, not lost one).
Step 6: Record revision in the session catalogue with provenance: which instance triggered the revision.
upward_revision_protocol.constraint: Upward revision is blocked if any existing declared instance would fail the proposed novel invariant. The novel invariant would then be a distinguishing feature of S_instance relative to S_abstract, not a universal abstract property.

nos_self_application.title: INV-NOS-004 Applied to the AI Edition Itself
nos_self_application.description: The AI Edition is an abstract structure. Each book is a declared instance. INV-NOS-004 demands that every book satisfy the invariants declared at the series level (AI_Edition_module.json). Book 8 applies this self-referentially: it uses NoS-Κ to audit the series for abstraction consistency.

declared_series_invariants: Every book must have a unique book_id with no path dashes
Every book must declare session_context = rtt=1 | coherence=declared | drift=bounded | paradox=structural
Every book must have qmroot_binding at 0D
Folder naming must use underscores, not dashes
Repo owner is umaywant2 — no other owner identifiers in canonical paths

nos_self_application.self_application_note: Any file in the AI Edition that violates a series-level invariant is, under INV-NOS-004, either a modeling error (must be corrected) or a genuine novelty (the series abstract must be revised). Drift — detected throughout the session history — is the manifestation of AC-OUT-002 (Modeling Error) at the series level. Book 8's role as capstone is to name this formally: drift is not aesthetic; it is an abstraction consistency violation.
